class.noble.ISL: a house of emirs and viziers
class.craftsman.family.ISL: into the family of a bazaar craftsman
class.landowner.family.ISL: into the family of a landed notable
prof.farmer.desc.ISL: A field by the canal, date palms, a tax on the harvest and the endless hope for water.
prof.laborer.desc.ISL: Bales on your back, bricks on a building site, any work for a day's pay.
prof.artisan.desc.ISL: Coppersmiths, tanners, glassblowers: every craft has its own row in the bazaar and its own headman.
prof.weaver.desc.ISL: Linen, silk, carpets and fine cloth that merchants carry overseas.
prof.midwife.desc.ISL: You are called into homes where men may not go: births, women's ailments, herbs.
prof.merchant.desc.ISL: A shop in the bazaar, letters of credit, goods from India and China. You may grow rich — or go bankrupt.
prof.sailor.desc.ISL: Boats on the river, ships on the Mediterranean and the Indian Ocean. Dangerous, but the pay is decent.
prof.soldier.desc.ISL: Service in the army of a caliph, sultan or emir: pay, campaigns and the risk of never coming back.
prof.scribe.desc.ISL: A reed pen, ink and paper. Books, letters, contracts — literate people are valued.
prof.physician.desc.ISL: You heal by the books of Galen and Ibn Sina and serve in a bimaristan hospital. Honoured and well paid.
prof.priest.desc.islam: You lead prayers at the neighbourhood mosque, give the Friday sermon and teach children the Qur'an.
prof.priest.desc.christian: You serve your community's church: liturgy, baptisms, funerals and the parish's worries.
prof.priest.desc.judaism: You teach Torah, settle the community's disputes and lead prayer in the synagogue.
prof.priest.desc.zoroastrian: You keep the sacred fire and the rites of an old faith that grows smaller every year.
prof.landholder.desc.ISL: Lands and tenant fellahin, and under the Seljuks and Mamluks the iqta: the right to a land's revenue in return for service.
prof.magistrate.desc.ISL: A judge of sharia: inheritances, marriages, debts and disputes. Power, respect and dangerous requests from the mighty.
prof.matron.desc.ISL: The women's quarters of a great house: maids, stores, weddings, the family's money.
prof.household_slave.desc.ISL: Work in the master's house. Freeing a slave is held to be a pious deed — there is hope.
prof.field_slave.desc.ISL: Hard labour in fields, canals and salt flats.
prof.officer.desc.ISL: A troop of horsemen rides under your banner. Pay, an iqta and the envy of other emirs.
prof.officer.desc.istanbul: Commander of a Janissary company — literally "the soup-giver". The company's cauldron is its banner.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.ISL: Your own workshop in the bazaar row, apprentices and a voice in the guild.
prof.shipowner.desc.ISL: Your own vessels, shares in caravans and letters of credit from Seville to Aden.
prof.official.desc.ISL: Service in the chancery: tax registers, seals and other people's fates in your scrolls.
prof.overseer.desc.ISL: A slave trusted by the master with the household and the other servants.
prof.muezzin.desc: Five times a day you climb the minaret and call the city to prayer. You need a strong, beautiful voice.
prof.caravaneer.desc: You lead camels across the desert from well to well, caravanserai to caravanserai. Profitable and dangerous.
prof.mamluk.desc: A slave-soldier bought as a boy. Years of training — horse, bow, lance — then freedom and service to your master.
prof.janissary.desc: The sultan's infantry: barracks, the company cauldron, pay and strict rules. A force even viziers fear.
prof.astronomer.desc: Astrolabe, zij tables, reckoning prayer times and the direction of Mecca. Rulers also expect horoscopes.
prof.perfumer.desc: Rose water, musk, ambergris and aloeswood. Your shop scents the whole bazaar row.
prof.coffee_keeper.desc: Copper pots, backgammon, poets and gossip. A new trade, and the authorities eye it with suspicion.
focus.learn.desc.ISL: The maktab: reading, writing and sums. The family pays the teacher
focus.study.desc.ISL: Madrasa, books, lessons with famous scholars. Costs money
focus.health.desc.ISL: The hammam, rest, herbs and walks in gardens
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.ISL: Rice, mutton, fruit, sherbets. Good for health
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.ISL: Feasts of dozens of dishes, sweets, guests and fame. Expensive
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.ISL: Riding, archery, polo. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.ISL: Prayers, verse amulets, the tombs of saints
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.ISL: A learned physician watches over the family's health. Expensive, but fewer die
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.ISL: A jug of water and ablutions at home
lifestyle.baths.sometimes.desc.ISL: The hammam on Fridays and holidays
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.ISL: Steam, marble slabs, the neighbourhood's news. Must live in a city
ev.v_wine_symposium.text.ISL: Wine is forbidden, yet in a rich neighbour's garden it is quietly poured from jars bought at a Christian monastery. A poet recites verses about the cup, the guests laugh and drink ever faster.
ev.v_poppy_pain.text.ISL: An old pain in your lower back has kept you awake for months. The physician takes out a vial of dark poppy juice: "Five drops in sherbet at night. No more — it is treacherous."
ev.j_scr_papyrus.text.ISL: Good paper has gone up in price again. A merchant you know whispers that he can get you cheap sheets — no questions asked about where they came from.
ev.y_wax_tablet.text.ISL: You traced letters with a reed pen on a wooden board while the maktab teacher walked between the rows with a switch. But the board can be washed clean and you start again.
ev.w_tomb_visit.text.ISL: On Friday you went to the cemetery to the graves of your own, laid myrtle sprigs and said a prayer — so the dead would know they are remembered.
ev.contubernium.text.ISL: A slave may marry only with the master's permission. Your master allows you to live with the person you have grown attached to.
ev.y_procession_run.text.ISL: A festive procession is winding through the city: drums, banners, camels in bright trappings, and all the neighbourhood children are already there. You, meanwhile, have been told to stay home and sort lentils.
ev.j_mag_games.text.ISL: Your office demands generosity: for the feast you must feed the poor of the quarter and hand out clothes and sweets. The treasury gave a little, the rest comes from your own purse. People remember the generous and never forgive the stingy.
ev.j_mag_games_echo.text.ISL: Years later people still recall your generosity. Whole quarters speak for you to the vizier, and a new office brings you honour.
ev.w_old_lares.text.ISL: {npc} is now the keeper of the family's treasures: you yourself placed in {g=npc_sex:his|her} hands the old book of Scripture and the prayer beads your grandparents used.
ev.j_mat_festival.text.ISL: The women of the quarter have chosen you to host a great festive evening. A great honour, but costly: sweets, lamps, singers with tambourines.
ev.festival.text.ISL: The city is celebrating: lanterns in the streets, sweets, storytellers and songs until dawn.
prof.translator.desc.ISL: You translate the books of physicians, philosophers and astronomers from Greek and Syriac. The pay is gold, and the standards are strict.
